Start here

Welcome to AIT

We extend a warm welcome to all new students joining AIT. As the SOM Student Ambassadors (SSA), we've put this guide together to help you settle into campus life with ease and confidence — from your first official paperwork to finding your way around.

About SSA

“Lead with Unity, Progress with Action.” — SSA

The SOM Student Ambassadors (SSA) at AIT are a dedicated group of student representatives committed to fostering a supportive and collaborative environment within the School of Management. By facilitating communication between students and faculty, we help make sure the student voice is heard — offering academic guidance, organizing events, and creating opportunities for leadership development.

SSA's Purpose

Our core focus areas:

Support & Connect
Building an inclusive, collaborative student community through open communication and shared experiences.
Student Representation
A bridge between students and faculty, voicing concerns and suggestions that help shape programs and policies.
Mentorship
Peer academic guidance on course planning and program navigation.
Leadership & Development
Workshops, seminars, and networking events that build professional skills.
Events & Activities
Academic, cultural, and social events, including field trips, that foster community and holistic development.
First things first

Get Set Up

Mandatory paperwork, a working SIM, and a bank account — the three things to knock out in your first week.

Official Work Do this first

Submit necessary academic and official documents at the Student Affairs Center, Admissions Building.

Collect these documents

1 Accommodation Certificate Needed to open a bank account and for official registrations. Obtain from the AIT Accommodation Office. At Google Maps ↗
2 Student Certificate Issued by the OSA. Needed for visa extensions, bank account setup, and official documentation. At Google Maps ↗
3 Student ID Card Collect from the OSA. Used for bank account, campus access, AITCC discounts, library entry, and more. At Google Maps ↗
4 Medical Insurance Card Provided after registration also by OSA. Required for healthcare at the AIT Medical Center and affiliated hospitals. At Google Maps ↗

Also visit

GRU Government Relations Unit For immigration: visa extensions, 90-day reporting, residence notifications. Located in the Administration Building. At Google Maps ↗
$ Cashier Get your tuition invoice/receipt. Exchange rate changes may cause slight under- or overpayments. At Google Maps (Next to GRU) ↗

School Layout

SIM Cards & Connectivity

Get a Thai SIM card soon after arrival. Top-up balance typically covers both internet and calls, depending on the plan.

Popular providers

  • TrueMove H (most used by students)
  • AIS
  • dtac

Where to buy

  • 7-Eleven outlets
  • Future Park Mall
  • Airport kiosks
Required document: Passport
SSA recommendation: the dtac/TRUE 7-Eleven SIM is a solid default to start with — from ฿199 for 30GB/month, and you can buy it at any 7-Eleven, including the one on campus. Details: true.th — dtac/TRUE 7-Eleven SIM. Worth comparing against current AIS/TrueMove plans too, since promos change often.

Banking & Money Matters

Banking

Opening a Thai bank account is highly recommended — it makes paying tuition, rent, and QR transactions much easier.

Nearby banks: Kasikorn Bank (KBank), Siam Commercial Bank (SCB)

Required: Passport, accommodation & student certificates, and student ID.

Money exchange

Local banks and licensed exchange services often offer more competitive rates than the airport.

  • 1
    KBank & SCB (TUH Branch)Closest option to AIT — right by Thammasat University Hospital, before you even get to Future Park. Worth checking here first.
  • 2
    Oh Rich ExchangeFuture Park (2nd Floor). Often the more competitive rate, and you can transfer the exchanged amount straight into your Thai bank account there. Rates: ohrich.com/rate
Required: Passport and Thai mobile number.

ATMs on campus

Next to 7-Eleven (Bangkok Bank ATM)

Next to Hom Krun Coffee Shop (SCB Bank ATM)

Identify Notes & Coins

Transportation

Get Around

From campus bicycles to the BTS Skytrain — how to actually get where you're going.

Public Buses

Affordable and convenient, though frequent stops can slow things down during busy times.

Pick-up point: AIT Bus Stop, near the main gate (Gate 1) · Running 5am–11pm

  • 510 — to Future Park, Don Mueang Airport (DMK), Victory Monument, etc.
  • 39 — to Future Park, BTS Yaek Kor Por Aor Station, etc.
Use the ViaBus app to track real-time bus location. Route info: transitbangkok.com
Open AIT Bus Stop in Google Maps ↗

Vans

Faster than buses, with fewer stops — ideal for quicker intercity travel, at a slightly higher cost.

Pick-up point: Thammasat Van Terminal

Popular destinations: Future Park, Victory Monument, Bangkok terminals

Open Thammasat Van Terminal ↗

Taxis & Ride-Hailing

Taxis run on a meter — fare isn't known until arrival. Ride-hailing apps are convenient; note they strictly enforce passenger limits.

Apps: Grab, Bolt · Pay with cash or mobile payment

Both apps work well around AIT — worth having both installed and comparing fares.

Anywheel Bikes & Scooters

Green bikes parked around campus — rent them easily through the Anywheel app.

How to use

  • 1
    Download the Anywheel App
  • 2
    Top up via TrueMoney or debit/credit card
  • 3
    Enable Bluetooth and GPS on your phone
  • 4
    Scan the QR code on the bike to unlock it
  • 5
    Park only at designated areas — lock manually, then scan the parking-spot QR to end your trip

Rates: Bike — ฿10 unlock + ฿10/30 min · Scooter — ฿15 unlock + ฿3/min

An Anywheel bike parked near the dorms

Metro Systems

The fastest way to move around the city and avoid traffic — but pricier than other options.

  • BTS Skytrain (Sukhumvit Line) — closest station Yaek Kor Por Aor, reachable via bus No. 39
  • MRT (Metro) — covers major Bangkok areas
  • ARL (Airport Rail Link) — connects to both DMK and Suvarnabhumi Airports

Bangkok Metropolitan Rapid Transit Network — design © 2025 Oran Viriyincy

Getting tickets

  • Select your destination on the route map at the vending machine
  • Up to 4 tickets per transaction on BTS, 10 on MRT (default is 1)
  • Payment: QR, coins (1/2/5/10 baht); some machines accept banknotes
  • Tap in at entry, insert/drop at exit — keep your ticket until you're out
Rabbit Cards (BTS) and MRT stored-value cards can be topped up at machines or counters. During busy hours, buy at the station counter instead.
Day to day

Campus Life

Where to eat, do laundry, see a doctor, and unwind between classes.

Bicycles on Campus

The main way to get around campus.

Where to buy

  • Junk to Jade (Facebook group) — secondhand bikes from students/staff
  • On-campus cycle repair shop
  • Online shops

Air filling stations: at the cycle repair shop, and near Laundry.

Shops Inside Campus

7-Eleven — food, snacks, toiletries, mobile top-ups, basic medicines. Cash & TrueMoney only. Open 24/7, delivery via app.

AIT Grocery Store — fresh produce, snacks, dairy, frozen food. 8am–10pm daily.

AIT Bookstore — stationery, snacks, books, AIT merchandise.

Eating & Drinking

On-campus options:

  • Somtam Canteen (Thai & international variety)
  • Tan90 (coffee, fast bites)
  • Waterview (Thai meals)
  • UFM Bakery (pastries and drinks)
  • Hom Krun Coffee (great for studying)
  • Tao Bin (AI vending machine)
  • ...and more
Water dispensers: ฿1/liter (accepts ฿1/2/5/10 coins) — plus free water stations at academic buildings and dorms.

Campus Services

Laundry

  • In dorms: washing machines in many student units
  • Washing Point B2: self-service laundry (฿10 discount every Wednesday)
  • LADA Laundry — opposite AIT Grocery

Self-service machines only accept ฿10 coins — coin machine available at B2 Washing Point.

Second-hand items

Students sell belongings each semester on the Junk to Jade Facebook group — bicycles, furniture, kitchenware, electronics, and more at reasonable prices. Highly recommended for new students furnishing a room.

Other services

  • Prayer room
  • Photocopy & printing shops
  • Hair salon in AIT Arcade
  • Massage spa in AIT Arcade

Health Care & Medical

AIT Medical Clinic — consultations, medication, vaccinations. Walk-in or appointment.

Thammasat University Hospital — advanced diagnostics and specialist treatment. Accepts medical insurance.

AIT's medical insurance covers up to ฿2,500/year.

Sports & Study Spots

Sports: Football, basketball, tennis, table tennis, cricket, golf. Swimming pool 8am–6:30pm.

Gym: ฿200/month, register at Student Affairs.

Study spots: Library, and the SOM Lounge — a relaxed space for SOM students to study, watch movies, or hang out.

Deliveries: parcels usually to AIT Square or Hom Krun Coffee · food delivery to Gate 2.

All Places, on One Map

Every location mentioned in this guide — bus stop, offices, banks, malls, markets — bundled into one file. Download it and import into Google My Maps to get them all pinned at once, instead of tapping through this page one place at a time.

  1. Download the file below.
  2. Go to google.com/mymaps → Create a new map.
